title: Understanding the Holy Spirit
description: Follow what Scripture says about the Holy Spirit — from creation and the prophets, through Jesus' promise and Pentecost, to the Spirit's work in believers and the church.
objectives: See how the Holy Spirit is described across the Old and New Testaments
Understand Jesus' promise of the Spirit and its fulfilment at Pentecost
Consider the Spirit's work in believers and in the church

sessions.title: The Spirit at creation and in Israel
sessions.intro: The Spirit appears in Scripture's first verses, and later comes upon the elders who help Moses lead.

questions.text: What is the Spirit of God doing in Genesis 1:2?
In Numbers 11, why does Moses need help, and what happens when the Spirit comes on the seventy elders?
What does Moses' wish in Numbers 11:29 suggest about how widely the Spirit might one day be given?

sessions.title: The promise through the prophets
sessions.intro: The prophets look forward to a day when God will put his Spirit within his people and pour it out on all kinds of people.

questions.text: What does God promise to do in Ezekiel 36:26-27?
In Joel 2:28-29, who receives the Spirit? What is significant about that list?
These promises were given to Israel in times of exile and judgement. What hope do they hold out?

sessions.title: The Spirit and Jesus
sessions.intro: The Spirit descends on Jesus at his baptism, leads him into the wilderness, and Jesus announces his mission in the Spirit's power.

questions.text: What happens at Jesus' baptism in Luke 3:21-22?
How often is the Spirit mentioned in Luke 4:1-18? What does that emphasise?
In Luke 4:18-19, Jesus reads from Isaiah. What does the Spirit anoint him to do?

sessions.title: Born of the Spirit
sessions.intro: Jesus tells Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel, that no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.

supporting.note: 'Born again / from above' in the original

questions.text: Who is Nicodemus, and when does he come to Jesus?
What does Jesus mean by being 'born of water and the Spirit' (verse 5)? What do the following verses add?
What does the comparison with the wind in verse 8 suggest about the Spirit's work?

sessions.title: Another Helper
sessions.intro: On the night before his death, Jesus promises his disciples that the Father will send the Spirit.

questions.text: What names and descriptions does Jesus use for the Spirit in these passages?
List what Jesus says the Spirit will do in John 14:26 and 16:8-15.
Why does Jesus say in 16:7 that it is good for the disciples that he goes away?

sessions.title: Pentecost
sessions.intro: Fifty days after the resurrection, the Spirit is poured out on the disciples in Jerusalem, and Peter explains what is happening.

questions.text: Describe what happens in Acts 2:1-4 and how the crowd reacts.
Which prophecy does Peter quote in verses 16-21, and how does it connect with what you read in Joel?
What does Peter tell the crowd to do in verse 38, and what does he promise?

sessions.title: Life by the Spirit
sessions.intro: Paul describes believers as people in whom the Spirit of God lives, led by the Spirit as God's children.

questions.text: According to verses 9-11, what difference does the Spirit's presence make?
What does the Spirit enable believers to call God in verse 15?
What does verse 16 say the Spirit testifies to?

sessions.title: The fruit of the Spirit
sessions.intro: Paul contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit the Spirit produces.

questions.text: What does Paul tell the Galatians to do in verses 16 and 25?
Paul speaks of the 'fruit' (singular) of the Spirit in verses 22-23. What might that word suggest about how these qualities grow?
Which quality in verses 22-23 would you most like to understand better, and why?

sessions.title: Gifts for the common good
sessions.intro: Writing to a divided church, Paul explains that the Spirit gives different gifts to different people for the good of all.

questions.text: What was happening in the Corinthian church that led Paul to write about spiritual gifts?
Who gives the gifts, and for what purpose (verses 4-7, 11)?
What does the picture of one body in verses 12-13 teach about believers' different gifts?

sessions.title: Sealed and filled
sessions.intro: Paul describes the Spirit as God's seal and guarantee, warns against grieving the Spirit, and urges believers to be filled with the Spirit.

questions.text: What do the words 'seal' and 'deposit' or 'guarantee' (1:13-14) suggest about the Spirit's role?
What does Paul say not to do in 4:30, and what surrounds that verse in 4:25-32?
What does being filled with the Spirit look like in 5:18-20?
